cells.tense: You are here, and your own account of what the tellers left you is clear.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, what you actually believe now — the ground under a habit you still keep.
cells.core:
The tellers did their work, and you know what came back from it. Your own account of the line you were handed is clear and in the room with you when you speak it. You are the one who decides what gets passed on, not loudest and not a passenger, just the hand that picks.

That aliveness is not busyness. It is the account already made, held loosely, room left for the next person to bring something. This is the edge worth guarding: keep it a conversation with what proved real rather than a monument to it. There is nothing to defend in the picking. The one option this balance frees is to feed what is next — say the line in the terms that belong to you, and let that be enough.

cells.tense: You are writing the moment your account is finally settled and you become its authority.
cells.ask: Give the next answer in three sentences and leave the fourth unsaid.
cells.core:
Held well, you tell the account and receive it again in the same breath, and the telling stays both a conversation and yours. What is happening now is that you're pushing the account harder than anyone asked. Get it finished, get the version nobody can amend, and the next exchange turns into a chance to hand it over whole. The pushing has replaced receiving it fresh.

What's ahead is a room with no one left in it to hear the thing again. The finish you're working toward closes the account to keep it safe, which shuts down what keeps it alive. Let the question stand unanswered once and see what it does.

cells.tense: You were at the point your account could have been made and have not been back since.
cells.ask: Tell the whole story to one person once — dates and the unfinished end — and leave it at exactly that.
cells.core:
The account of what you were given hasn't been finished. Somewhere behind is where making it would have happened, and you're still in the room before it. The retained possibility is not neutral now — it is heavy the way any creation put off is heavy.

No one stands there waiting for it to be declared. The sharing was interrupted, not the matter. What you were given was received; the making of it stopped. Carried well, the account gets spoken and the speaker is not braced for a verdict. Start by really letting one person's account land, even slightly wrong, and let the joining happen on its own. What opens a way back is being willing to receive, not to produce.
cells.sheetLine: The account is received and unmade, and the unfinished part is heavy.

cells.tense: You are already holding the account in this room and speaking of it as if it belonged to nobody.
cells.ask: Name one piece of what you believe, in the first person, without crediting anyone first.
cells.core:
You already carry what the tradition means — how you put things, what you take up again, what you let pass without comment. People you talk with are getting your version and shaping theirs accordingly. The running is happening, and you still talk about the whole thing as if it were the signal's.

The block is between the running and the credit. One sentence of origin would fuse it into view. Said well, the person telling the thing and the person hearing it are the same person. "This is what I believe the tradition means" — said plainly, once. The stream is yours, and the joining is saying so.

attempts.check: The record supports direction already chosen in this seat, not that it always came back well. A reader could reasonably say the teaching was worn by the tellers rather than carried by them — that is the ground to cover without asserting it. The ask holds either way, because seeing one line run from its first hearing to the telling is useful whether or not my read is right. The sentence that serves me rather than the person is the one that declares the account already made; the house is sitting with what came back, not concluding.
